Independent exact replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/lehmer_two_ended.py (NumPy integer arithmetic). Checked degrees 20–34 unrestricted, 20–38 self-reciprocal and 20–41 antireciprocal, in batches of at most 16 left prefixes for the unrestricted pairings. All five printed vectors match frozen RESULT.md.
correctness.rationale: G=L² is monic and reciprocal of degree 20 with constant term one. For exact degree D, normalize the sign by Q(0)=1. Division, or coefficient comparison starting at the constant term, gives the unique quotient H of degree e=D−20; each trit prefix uniquely fixes the corresponding quotient prefix. Since G*=G, cancellation gives Q*=±Q iff H*=±H. In the self-reciprocal case at D=38 one enumerates a_1..a_9 and mirrors the resulting quotient through its midpoint, and at D=41 antireciprocity one enumerates a_1..a_10 and reflects with sign. The unrestricted proof covers all 3^14 trit prefixes with a nonzero lead check. The frozen program's exact convolution gates all degrees; a conservative recurrence bound gives every intermediate convolution absolute sum at most 137789545, so the integer type suffices. I independently recomputed G from L and ran a two-ended exact enumeration: for the unrestricted class it chooses trits from both ends (including both leading signs) to determine disjoint quotient sections, then explicitly checks every remaining product coefficient. For the symmetry classes it mirrors the quotient and handles a forced zero middle for even antireciprocal degrees. Bound-checked signed integer arithmetic gives no solutions below the respective thresholds and exactly the five normalized vectors printed in the record at the thresholds. The degree-34 vectors are reversals; reversal on the antireciprocal vectors stays within each sign pair. The exact signed counts are 4,2,4, and independent integer multiplication gives the self-reciprocal quotient factorization in the notes.
residual_risks: The computation is a finite integer exhaustion of these degree ranges; no inference for greater degrees, or other powers of L, is asserted.

Prior minimum-degree theorem and existence tables
value.rationale: The first permitted degrees for Lehmer-square divisibility are natural boundary parameters fixed by the prior theorem, not arbitrary slices. Their multiplicities distinguish a single orbit, uniqueness under the positive-reversal constraint, and two genuinely different antireciprocal sign classes, the last impossible to read off from a single witness and its reversal. Exact counts and representatives give a useful benchmark for algorithms or structural work on extremal restricted-coefficient multiples.
residual_risks: This is a precise finite classification and does not purport to give a general formula or a new theorem on the full degree spectrum.
